title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This integrated playbook documents Redwood Inference’s end-to-end applied ML evaluation process: onboarding new models into the eval-harness, curating and validating prompt sets & benchmarks, creating and validating quantization profiles, defining quality guardrails, and operating a regression triage workflow. The goal is to ensure consistent, repeatable model quality checks before and after deployment while enabling fast iteration and safe rollouts.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: model onboarding through post-deploy regression detection and triage for text generation, chat, and embedding models used on the Redwood platform. Includes guidance for the eval-harness, prompt sets, quantization test matrices, and incident triage.
- Audience: applied ML engineers, model-onboarding owners, SREs responsible for monitoring eval signals, and product engineers running integration tests.

Goals and success criteria:
- Automated eval coverage for each onboarded model that exercises representative production prompt sets (target >= 95% of critical flows).
- Quantization profiles validated such that end-user visible metric regressions are within agreed thresholds (see "Quality Guardrails").
- Regression alerting that has mean time to triage (MTTT) < 4 hours and clear escalation paths.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: Applied ML Platform (team: engineering) — Maya Patel.
- Evaluation infra: Eval-Harness team — Diego Ramirez.
- Quantization and kernel testing: Serving Runtime team — Sofia Chen.
- On-call triage: Eng SRE rotations; escalation to Applied ML on-call.

Prerequisites for onboarding a model:
1) Model artifact and spec (format: HF or ONNX with metadata.json).
2) Baseline eval run on unquantized model: standard eval-harness run using canonical prompt sets.
3) Performance profile: median p95 latency, memory footprint, and throughput on supported hardware.
4) Risk assessment doc (sensitivity, PII exposure risk, regulatory constraints).

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1. Create model entry in the model catalog with owner, expected traffic, and privacy classification.
2. Run baseline eval-harness job: reference suite = core_prompt_set_v1 (see Prompt Set section). Record metrics: accuracy/F1, ROUGE/BLEU where applicable, perplexity, embedding cosine similarity distributions, and hallucination score.
3. Upload raw eval artifacts to benchmarks-bucket (S3 path) and link to model entry.
4. If performance targets unmet, iterate with model owner and runtime team (kernel/quantization changes).
5. Approve for staged serving only after passing quality guardrails.

Prompt sets and benchmarks:
- Prompt taxonomy: critical flows, edge cases, adversarial cases, and hallucination-sensitive cases.
- Standard canonical prompt sets: core_prompt_set_v1, embeddings_probe_v1, safety_and_misinfo_v2.
- Benchmarks storage: S3://redwood-evals/benchmarks/<model-id>/<run-timestamp> with manifest.json listing input prompts, expected outputs, and scoring rules.
- Prompt set curation process:
  1. Product/feature owners nominate representative prompts.
  2. Applied ML curates and annotates expected outputs or scoring heuristics.
  3. QA runs synthetic and manual validation and signs off.
- Benchmarking cadence: full suite run nightly for active models; smoke tests on each commit.

Quality guardrails and pass/fail thresholds:
- Primary metrics and thresholds (default):
  - Generation quality: pass if aggregate semantic similarity to reference set >= 0.78 (embedding cosine mean).
  - Safety: no more than 0.01% high-severity safety violations on safety_and_misinfo_v2.
  - Hallucination: hallucination-rate delta vs baseline < 2 percentage points.
  - Perplexity: relative increase < 1.15 for instruction models.
  - Embeddings: mean cosine similarity vs baseline >= 0.985 after quantization for embedding models.
  - Latency: p95 token generation <= service SLO (example 250ms for small models, 800ms for large models on Dedicated pool).
- Pass/fail policy:
  - Automatic block: any safety violation > threshold -> block deployment and trigger immediate triage.
  - Soft regressions: metrics outside guardrail but within tolerance generate a regression alert and require owner acknowledgment before rollout.

Quantization profiles: creation and validation workflow:
1. Profile candidate configs: per-layer quantization strategy (e.g., 8-bit asymmetric, 4-bit, group-wise quant). Record size, expected speedup, and initial accuracy delta.
2. Create a quantization-profile YAML with fields: profile_id, model_id, hw_target, quant_scheme, calibration_dataset, known_issues.
   Example snippet:
   ---
   profile_id: qprof-gpt2-med-8bit-v1
   model_id: model-gpt2-medium-v3
   hw_target: a100-40gb
   quant_scheme: int8-asymmetric
   calibration_dataset: core_prompt_set_v1
   known_issues: []
   ---
3. Run validation suite: full eval-harness with calibration and post-quant eval. Collect metric deltas and performance numbers.
4. If the profile passes guardrails, incrementally enable in staging under a canary policy (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Monitor eval-signal and A/B metrics.
5. If a soft regression appears during canary, rollback profile and open a quantization bug with Serving Runtime.

Regression detection and triage playbook:
Detection:
- Sources of regression signals: nightly benchmark runs, production shadow runs, user-reported issues, and automated canary A/B tests.
- Alerting thresholds: any metric crossing guardrail publishes an alert to #applied-ml-alerts and creates an issue in the regression-triage queue.

Triage procedure (ordered):
1. Triage lead (on-call Applied ML) acknowledges alert within 30 minutes.
2. Gather context: model version, recent commits, quantization profile id, rollout fraction, recent eval artifacts, and any related infra events.
3. Reproduce with eval-harness locally using the failing prompt subset.
4. Classify regression: performance, quality (semantic drift), safety, or infrastructure.
5. If safety or severe quality regression -> immediate rollback and paging to product security and SRE.
6. If performance/regression due to quantization -> mark profile as blocked and assign to Serving Runtime.
7. For minor regressions, open a remediation plan: owner, ETA, test plan, and temporary mitigations (rate limit, fallback model).
8. Document root cause and postmortem for any regression that required rollback.

Operational runbook and automation hooks:
- Playbook automation: eval-harness jobs are scheduled via cron (k8s CronJob) and can be triggered manually via eval-run CLI: eval-run --model <id> --suite core_prompt_set_v1 --output s3://...
- Canary automation: Service control plane supports rollout policies. Use CLI: redwood rollout start --model <id> --profile <qprof-id> --initial 1% --monitoring eval-metrics,ab-tests
- Alerting: PagerDuty integration for severity=critical; Slack channel #applied-ml-alerts for triage conversation.

Tables and example thresholds (text table):
- Quantization test matrix (text):
  | Profile | HW Target | Expected Size Reduction | Allowed Quality Delta | Canary Fraction |
  | qprof-gpt2-8bit | a100-40gb | 2.8x | <= 2% acc drop / embedding cosine >= 0.98 | 1% -> 100% |
  | qprof-gpt2-4bit | h100-80gb | 5x | <= 5% drop / manual review required | 0.5% -> 20% |

Key CLI examples:
- Run full eval: eval-run --model model-xyz --suite core_prompt_set_v1 --out s3://redwood-evals/benchmarks/model-xyz/2026-03-04
- Validate quant profile: eval-run --model model-xyz --quant-profile qprof-xyz --suite core_prompt_set_v1 --compare-to baseline://model-xyz/unquantized
- Start canary rollout: redwood rollout start --model model-xyz --profile qprof-xyz --initial 1% --monitoring eval-metrics

Decision rules for rollouts and rollbacks:
- Block rollout if safety metric fails at any canary stage.
- If soft regressions appear (metric delta > guardrail but < block threshold), pause rollout and require owner sign-off.
- Automatic rollback if user-visible degradation (error rate or top-line quality) > 3x of historical variance during canary.

Postmortem and learning loop:
- For every regression that triggers rollback, produce a 72-hour postmortem with: timeline, root cause, mitigation, owners, and follow-up action items.
- Maintain retro board of recurring failure modes and update prompt sets/guardrails accordingly.

Metrics, dashboards, and SLOs to track:
- Nightly eval pass rate (target >= 95%).
- Canary detection time (target < 15 minutes from first metric crossing).
- Mean time to triage (MTTT) < 4 hours.
- Regression recurrence rate (target < 5% per quarter).
- Dashboards: per-model eval metrics, quant-profile performance, canary rollouts, and safety violations per model.

Related pages and artifacts:
- eval-harness standards, prompt set catalog, quantization-profiles best practices, and regression triage queue. Links in Related Pages metadata above.

Appendix: common failure modes and mitigations (brief):
- Failure: calibration dataset mismatch -> Mitigation: expand calibration set to include long-tail prompts and re-run calibration.
- Failure: hallucination spike after quantization -> Mitigation: revert to unquantized profile or use hybrid (KV-cache unquantized) strategy.
- Failure: throughput regressions on specific kernel -> Mitigation: route to alternative kernel via runtime config and open kernel ticket.

This playbook is a living document. Review cadence: quarterly or after any major regression incident. For questions or process exceptions, contact the Applied ML Platform owner listed above.
